results.title: Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin to announce presidential bid
results.content: France’s former conservative prime minister Dominique de Villepin, who served as former president Jacques Chirac’s foreign minister during the country’s steadfast opposition to the US-led invasion of Iraq in 2003, is expected to formally launch his presidential campaign Friday. But while De Villepin’s opposition to Israel’s Gaza campaign and assured analysis of international affairs has caught the eyes of younger voters, it remains to be seen if he can persuade them to cast a ballot for him.

results.title: Iraqi security forces deploy in Hezbollah stronghold under compromise deal
results.content: Iraqi security forces deployed ​in the Kataib Hezbollah stronghold of Jurf al-Sakhar, state media said on Friday, under a compromise deal brokered by Shi'ite politicians. Iraq's prime minister ordered a security intervention earlier this week after accusing the Iran-backed militia of smuggling state-owned oil worth ⁠hundreds of millions of dollars.

results.title: Europe's youth set to join mass cost of living protests in 25 countries
results.content: Youth protests are set to take place in more than 25 countries in Europe on Friday and over the weekend, coalition organisers said, as demostrators seek to increase pressure on governments over issues including soaring housing costs and deteriorating learning conditions with a show of cross-border solidarity.

results.title: 🔴 Live: Deadly Russian attacks damage two bridges in Kyiv, mayor says
Live: Several killed, dozens wounded in Russian attacks that damaged two Kyiv bridges
results.content: Russian attacks on Ukraine killed eight people and woulded 28, Ukraine's Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi ​said on ‌Friday. The fresh wave of missile and drone attacks – which also damaged two bridges in Kyiv – came after Russian President Vladimir Putin vowed a "painful" retaliation after Ukraine this week damaged the Crimea bridge. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

results.title: Infantino, Tashima and Diallo officially enter FIFA presidential race
results.content: Three candidates have officially submitted their bids for the FIFA presidency. Gianni Infantino, who has been in office for 11 years, is seeking a fourth consecutive term. Backed by UEFA, French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo wants to offer an alternative to Infantino’s leadership. He will face Japan’s Kozo Tashima, honorary president of the Japan Football Association. The election will take place on March 18, 2027 in Rabat, Morocco.

results.title: Czechs protest en masse against 'concentration of power in one hand' and growing control over media
results.content: As large demonstrations in the Czech Republic challenge Prime Minister Andrej Babiš's plans to change the funding model of public broadcasters, Mikuláš Minář, Chair of the Million Moments for Democracy movement, joins François Picard from Prague for Spotlight, warning that his country risks following Hungary and Slovakia in democratic backsliding. "We are really afraid that the Czech Republic is following the Orbánian Hungarian way, (Fico's) Slovakian way," he says.

results.title: EU and UK set to sign deals on trade, energy, youth mobility at Brussels summit
results.content: The UK and the EU are poised to agree new deals on trade, energy and youth mobility at a summit in Brussels on Friday, as part of UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's bid to reset ties with the bloc. Burnham – who has said he hopes to see Britain rejoin the EU in his lifetime – argues the deals will help fix some of the damage Brexit inflicted.

results.title: White House fires national cyber director over widespread outages
results.content: The White House fired national cyber director Sean Cairncross on Thursday following a week of technology disruptions affecting US air travel, email services and national security systems. The departure comes as the Trump administration faces criticism over its response to the outages, which officials say were unrelated incidents.

results.title: PM Sanchez admits 'mistakes' in key debate ahead of Spain's election
results.content: Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez acknowledged shortcomings in his government on Thursday as he faced conservative rival Alberto Nunez Feijoo in the campaign's only televised debate. The November 29 election could leave the far-right Vox party in a position to enter government.

results.title: Voyager 1 spacecraft reaches one light-day milestone
results.content: NASA's Voyager 1 probe, which has been traveling through space for nearly 50 years, hit a milestone distance of one light-day away from Earth on Wednesday. Already the most distant man-made object in the universe, the spacecraft is now about 26 billion kilometers (16 billion miles) away, according to the US space agency. That is the distance a particle of light can travel in 24 hours. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

results.title: Armed forces in Haiti kill at least 34 gang members to regain control of key corridor
results.content: Haitian security forces launched a major offensive on Thursday to retake Martissant, a strategic corridor linking Port-au-Prince with the country's western and southern regions that gangs have controlled for five years. Police said at least 34 suspected gang members were killed in clashes involving a private security task force.

results.title: Anthropic goes public after blockbuster IPO but fails to revive AI trade
results.content: Anthropic has become the first pure-play AI developer to be publicly traded on the stock market, following a record-setting IPO. The stock opened 34 percent higher, briefly valuing the company at more than $2 trillion, before ending its first day of trading up 17 percent. However, Wall Street indexes closed sharply lower as investors took profits, reflecting underlying market jitters about the AI trade.

results.title: French far-left candidate Mélenchon opens door to alliance with rival Greens candidate
results.content: French far-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon opened the door to an alliance with France's Greens on Thursday after their presidential candidate Marine Tondelier said she was ready to "work on a coalition around" the veteran leftist. Tondelier's overture has further boosted Mélenchon's campaign for the Élysée Palace – and angered moderates on the centre-left.

results.title: Kenyan marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir banned for doping
results.content: In tonight's edition: Kenyan athletics superstar and reigning marathon world champion Peres Jepchirchir is banned for three years for doping. Also, South African judges leave the courtroom behind and tour a repatriation centre before handing down judgment in 33 emergency asylum applications. Plus Ghana's presidency has a new jet, but critics of the ruling party are not on board.

results.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv kill one, damage Dutch and Austrian embassies
results.content: A wave of daytime Russian strikes on Kyiv on Thursday killed one person and damaged a historic cathedral as well as the embassies of Austria and the Netherlands. Loud explosions erupted across the Ukraine capital throughout the day as the leaders of Russia, China and the United States held a historic meeting in China that put Russia's President Vladimir Putin in international spotlight. FRANCE 24's Laurent Berstecher reports.

results.title: 'We're seeing in real time the effects that AI is going to have on cybersecurity', expert says
results.content: FRANCE 24's Monte Francis speaks with Dr. R. David Edelman, Senior Fellow at the Brookings Institution, also former Director for Cybersecurity on the National Security Council under the Obama administration. He explains that the latest spate of network outages shows "in real time the effects that AI is going to have on cybersecurity" adding that "the one thing that's tying most of these outages together is that companies and institutions are racing to patch a system that's been identified as vulnerable, and they're patching what themselves are pretty creaky digital systems".

results.title: Kushner says Trump 'open' to extend NATO mutual defense-type clause to Ukraine
results.content: US envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday that President Donald Trump was open to extending to Ukraine a security guarantee similar to NATO's mutual defense clause, but stressed that Washington has to protect its interests too. The comments came as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz qualified the summit between the presidents of the United States, Russia and China as a "photo op". FRANCE 24's international affairs commentator Douglas Herbert explains.

results.title: Macron urges Ukraine's allies to 'reopen the question' of NATO membership
results.content: French President Emmanuel Macron on Thursday called for Ukraine's allies to speed up the delivery of urgently needed air defence systems and urged them to "reopen the question" of Ukraine's NATO membership after talks in Berlin aimed at reaffirming European support for Kyiv.

results.title: A president among body bags: Photo ops spark outrage in Colombia
results.content: Since taking office in August, Colombia's far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella has regularly posted videos that show him walking among body bags supposedly holding the remains of rebel fighters – a communications strategy that has sparked widespread criticism.

results.title: Three of a kind? Xi hosts Trump and Putin as Ukraine war grinds on
results.content: Gang of three or glorified photo op? Xi Jinping hosting Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Already, our Monday panel rejected attempts to paint the three-way meeting as a new Yalta, as in the 1945 sit-down on the Black Sea that defined the post-war security architecture of Europe.

results.title: Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting: Trump's recognition of China and Russia as 'peers of the US'
results.content: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Olivia Cheung. The trilateral meeting between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit was significant despite the absence of concrete agreements, according to Cheung. “The significance is seen in the precedence of the United States seeing and giving recognition that China and Russia are peers of the United States,” she explained, adding that “the image of a G3 is very significant.”

results.title: NASA's Voyager 1 phones home from record one light-day away, 49 years after launch
results.content: The Voyager 1 probe launched by NASA nearly a half century ago has reached a distance from Earth of one light day (more than 26 billion kilometres), the farthest any human artifact has ever ventured from our planet. The space agency received a signal from the spacecraft Thursday, exactly 24 hours after it was sent.

results.title: French media regulator says it will monitor top YouTubers for bias in election coverage
results.content: Rules designed to safeguard media pluralism during elections campaigns will apply to France's most influential YouTubers in the run-up to next year's presidential contest, media regulator Arcom warned on Thursday, reflecting the growing influence of content creators whose audiences often outstrip those of traditional media companies.
